title: Continuous division by a uniformizer power
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, valuation topology, and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every $e\geq0$, multiplication by $\pi^e$ is a homeomorphism from $A$ onto the subspace $\pi^eA\subseteq E$. Consequently, if $T$ is a topological space and $f:T\to A$ is continuous with $f(t)\in\pi^eA$ for all $t$, there is a unique continuous $q:T\to A$ with $\pi^e q(t)=f(t)$. If $f(t_0)\in\pi^eA^\times$, then $q(t_0)\in A^\times$, and after restricting to an open neighbourhood of $t_0$, $q$ takes values in $A^\times$ and $q^{-1}$ is entrywise continuous.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite E case, pp. 18–19: continuous integral division and elementary pivot elimination; the displayed auxiliary statement is written out here because HRS uses it as a standard calculation.

proof.text: Specialize Padic.extension_integers_dvr to coefficientExtensionAbsoluteValue using spectralNorm_extends. Its chosen ring and maximal ideal are definitionally the recorded coefficient ring and maximal ideal. Extract the membership formulas, the criterion IsUnit a iff |a| = 1, nonzeroness of the maximal ideal, its uniformizer-generator equation, and the largest nonzero absolute value r in the maximal ideal. The generator equation and the nonzero maximal ideal show that the recorded uniformizer, and hence its e-th power c, is nonzero.

Equip E with the normed-field structure supplied by the recorded absolute value. Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero c gives the embedding x ↦ c*x of E. Compose with the subtype embedding of A, then apply Topology.IsEmbedding.toHomeomorph to obtain H : A ≃ₜ range (a ↦ c*a) with precisely the stated forward map. Lift f continuously into this range using its divisibility hypothesis, and define q by composing this lift with H.symm. The identity H.apply_symm_apply gives c*q(t)=f(t). Cancellation of c proves uniqueness among all quotients, even without using their continuity.

The maximal-value clause gives 0 ≤ r < 1 and says that every nonzero nonunit of A has absolute value at most r: a nonunit has absolute value below 1 and hence lies in the maximal ideal. Thus r < |a| implies that a is a unit. If f(t₀)=c*z for a unit z, cancellation gives q(t₀)=z, so |q(t₀)|=1. Take U={t | r < |q(t)|}; continuity of q and the absolute value makes U open, it contains t₀, and q is unit-valued throughout U. Apply ContinuousOn.inv₀ to the continuous E-valued map q, since its unit values are nonzero in E, to obtain the required continuous inverse on U.

proof_origin.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite E case, pp. 18–19; formalizes the existing division argument using the stated DVR maximal-value clause to exhibit an open unit neighbourhood.

I read the item in full: its statement and its 3 steps. The only node it cites is def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension: clause 1 (the absolute value), clause 2 (O_E and m_E = {|x|<1}) and clause 3 (uniformizer with pi O_E = m_E, so pi is nonzero). I also read the consumer lem-sfb-continuous-integral-pivot-splitting: its step 1 needs exactly the entrywise quotient, the unit at t0 and the local continuous inverse, and this statement gives all three. I read the unit sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors, the chapter sec-six-functors-basics, and the via chain up to lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves. Source: HRS arXiv 2305.18131, proof of Thm 6.12(2), pp. 18-19 ('Comparing valuations ... a,b in Gamma(S,O_E)'). That is the same division argument, and proof_origin=agent is correct because HRS does not state the unit or inverse clause. The statement is true. Multiplication by pi^e is a homeomorphism of E (inverse: multiplication by pi^{-e}) and restricts to a homeomorphism A -> pi^e A, so q is continuous and unique. If f(t0) = pi^e u then q(t0) = u by cancellation. A^x is open because u + m_E is the open unit ball and |u+m| = 1. Inversion is continuous on E^x because |x^-1 - y^-1| = |x-y|/(|x||y|). All three steps are correctly marked elementary, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Small cases checked: e=0; empty T; one-point T; f=0; E=Q_5, f(t)=5t, t0=1; f(t)=5t^2, t0=0, where q(0)=0 is not a unit, so the exact-valuation hypothesis is needed; changing the uniformizer only scales q by a constant unit. Duplicate search with rg: I read finite-continuous-ultrametric-pivot, continuous-field-matrix-elimination, integral-matrix-entry-properties and the coefficient nodes; none states this lemma, so same_as=[] is right. There are no new nodes, no route citation other than the definition, no tool_uses, no SGA source and no target or base-change morphism involved. Four Mathlib searches are recorded and I agree with 'no match'. Minor wording I did not change: 'entrywise continuous' is matrix wording carried over from the parent and here just means continuous; 'valuation topology' means the topology of |.|_E, as in the parent.
